text.insert: Each GameCube game supplies configuration, knowledge sources, and build artifacts to the shared harness. Grouped configuration and game-selected image planning are implemented. Acceptance still requires a real checkout, compilation and scoring evidence, and a verified Daytona claim for each new game.
Structure

rows: Shared harness
Worker lifecycle, claims, integration, tracing, and knowledge storage and retrieval.
Shared GameCube toolpack
Reusable compiler, disassembly, editing, and scoring implementations with explicit compatibility requirements.
Game definition
Repository and target version, build settings, tool bindings, external source definitions, and sandbox profiles.
Game-owned host state
Raw archives, knowledge database, search indexes, graph, runs, worktrees, and tool caches.
Game image and claim workspace
Compatible Linux tools, original inputs, matching compiler, built checkout, and claim revision delta.

text.insert: Use the tracked game descriptor as the entry point. Larger source scopes and tool settings can live in referenced game-owned files. Local overrides supply machine paths and credential references. Every consumer resolves the selected game explicitly; missing required configuration must not silently select Melee.
The Rule

rows: Repository, base ref, checkout, region or version, original input identities, and compiler pins.
The pinned checkout builds and emits the expected target report.
Enabled tools, build commands, object paths, and scoring settings.
Required tools pass capability checks; representative compilation and scoring agree with the host baseline.
PR, Discord, and wiki definitions with explicit enabled state and refresh policy.
Required sources have import manifests and resolvable sample citations. Disabled, unavailable, empty, and failed are distinct states.
Game-owned archive, database, graph, index, and cache paths.
Queries and writes remain inside the selected game, including concurrent runs for two games.
Sandbox image, baked revision, tool versions, workspace root, and resource profile.
A claim reaches its exact base revision, compiles one unit, returns evidence, and cleans up.

text.insert: External Source Contract

Each source instance identifies its game, kind, upstream identity, scope, adapter version, storage location, credential reference, and refresh policy. Acquisition commands should be shared implementations driven by these definitions.

rows: PRs
Repository owner/name, selection policy, and refresh cursor.
PR body, diff, review comments, issue comments, and stable capture identity.
Discord
Server and channel IDs, thread policy, and per-channel cursor.
Message IDs, authors, timestamps, thread context, and captured text.
Wiki
Site/API, adapter type, seed categories or pages, exclusions, and revision policy.
Canonical page identity, upstream revision, sections, and captured text.

text.insert: All three sources follow the same stages: acquisition, deterministic import, search indexing, and librarian curation. Report completion separately for each stage. Download success does not establish that records are searchable or facts are current.

Record the source instance, input manifest, cursor or revision, adapter version, counts, failures, and output identity for each stage. Rerunning an identical capture must not duplicate records or indexing work. Keep cited captures immutable; changed upstream text creates a new capture. Partial acquisition must not advance its cursor past missing material.

Scope identities and cursors by source instance and game. PR numbers collide across repositories, and page titles collide across wiki sites. Preserve cited evidence identities. Cross-game compiler knowledge requires explicit applicability and provenance.

Retain explicit wiki refresh as the initial policy because mirror imports are expensive. A common source contract does not require a common refresh schedule. Allow unavailable sources to be declared with a reason, while treating failure of a required source as a readiness failure.
Daytona Boundary

Knowledge queries use the selected game's store on the host. Raw knowledge corpora, the knowledge database, secrets, and orchestrator state stay outside the image. Each sandbox receives the tools and source artifacts required to compile and score its claim.

Use a reusable Linux tool layer and a game layer containing the configured checkout, original inputs, compiler versions, and baseline objects. Seed the claim from the recorded baked revision to its exact base revision. Incompatible compiler or build requirements, or an unavailable revision delta, require a newly accepted game image.

Track image provenance separately from knowledge provenance. A wiki refresh does not require an image rebuild. A new image does not overwrite knowledge. Each game configures its image workspace and host checkout independently.
Implementation and Acceptance

rows: Descriptor references load build, sandbox, tools, and source configuration. New games use grouped paths.
Existing Melee paths remain pinned. Live filesystem migration is a separate recoverable operation.
Named sandbox profiles retain 2-core and optional 4-core choices. Claims capture resolved image provenance.
Verify each configured image can execute and score the selected game before admitting real work.
Source definitions identify game, upstream, adapter, policy, and storage. Configured paths feed ingest.
Legacy ingest supports one enabled source per kind. Broader acquisition and source-isolated adapter coverage remain explicit limits.
Image bundle planning resolves game checkout, report path, tools, profile, and workspace.
The image recipe still assumes the supported GameCube build-artifact shape. A different build system needs an adapter.
The resolver preserves existing stores and rejects ambiguous default paths.
No second real game or new Daytona image has been established by configuration tests alone.

text.insert: Why

GameCube games can share most tool implementations while differing in compiler version, region, build conventions, and game-specific helpers. Explicit bindings and readiness checks make that reuse testable.

Make Melee the first complete instance, preserving melee-live and existing evidence identities. Validate the contract against a second named game before claiming portability. That checkout determines which differences belong in configuration and which require a build adapter.
